articles.title: ‘A long-time dream’: Nihal Sarin 'excited' but 'not thinking about' India's Chess Olympiad title defence
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: The Chess Olympiad is already on Indian Grandmaster Nihal Sarin’s mind, but not quite yet. With India preparing to defend its Open title in.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The Chess Olympiad is already on Indian Grandmaster Nihal Sarin’s mind, but not quite yet. With India preparing to defend its Open title in Samarkand, Uzbekistan later this month, Nihal is excited about representing the country at the Olympiad. For now, though, the 22-year-old is keeping his attention firmly on the Global Chess League (GCL), where he is representing American Gambits in this fourth season.Asked whether he was already thinking about the Olympiad while playing his games in Bengaluru, Nihal said: “Not really, no. Like, in general, I'm just extremely excited to play in the Olympiad. I'm very happy, and I'll just try to give my best for the team. It has been a long-time dream.”But with the GCL currently taking centre stage, Nihal is deliberately keeping things relaxed. “Now I'm just (focusing on GCL). This tournament is very relaxed. I'm just trying to chill on and off the board,” he said after American Gambits’ match against Ganges Grandmasters on Sunday.India’s title defence will carry considerable expectations. Four members of the Budapest-winning squad return, although there will understandably be significant changes to the board order. Arjun Erigaisi leads the five-player lineup on 2759, followed by Praggnanandhaa R on 2750. Nihal, rated 2718, will replace Pentala Harikrishna.World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju is also there, while Vidit Gujrathi completes the squad. Srinath Narayanan returns as captain.At the 2024 Olympiad in Budapest, Gukesh played on board one and delivered a phenomenal 9/10 score with a 3056 performance rating, winning individual gold as India finished four match points clear. Arjun also claimed individual gold on board three.Nevertheless, defending the title will be no easy task. Armenia remains the last team to successfully retain the Open crown, winning in 2006 and 2008. The last five editions have produced four different champions, underlining how difficult sustained dominance has been.What happened in GCL on Day 2 Defending champions APL Pipers made it two wins from two, beating Ganges Grandmasters 11-6, while Ganges bounced back later to defeat American Gambits 9-7. Nihal won his game against Levon Aronian with black pieces in a nerve-wracking battle, but it was not enough for his team. Alaskan Knights beat Mumba Masters 11-6, before Mumba Masters edged Triveni Continental Kings 10-9 in the final match of the day.At this moment, American Gambits lead the standings on 6 match points and 31 game points, ahead of Ganges Grandmasters on 6/25. Alpine APL Pipers are third with 6/21, while Mumba Masters and Alaskan Knights have 3 match points each. Continental Kings, the two-time champions, remain at the bottom without a win.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: TOI Exclusive: Personal coaches push gains momentum in equestrian, selectors’ dual roles raise questions
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games barely weeks away, a curious battle over coaches is brewing in Indian equestrian — five riders have sought accreditati.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games barely weeks away, a curious battle over coaches is brewing in Indian equestrian — five riders have sought accreditation for their foreign personal coaches, even as officials involved in selecting the team are themselves headed to Japan in coaching and team-management roles.The demand has put the spotlight on how the equestrian contingent’s coaching support was finalised, particularly because the foreign coaches being sought by the riders have trained them through the international season and are now being preferred over some of the Indian coaches cleared by the sports authorities.TOI has learnt that at least five of the seven dressage and eventing riders have sought to take their personal coaches to the Games. The five are Shruti Vora (athlete) — Rebecca Moody (British, coach); Ashish Limaye — Carola Bierlein (German); Gaurav Pundir — Brian Barnett (Dutch); Arjan Nagra — Felix Etzel (German); and Jai Sud — Antonie de Ridder (Dutch).All five have approached the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)-run ad-hoc committee for governance of the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), seeking accreditation for their personal coaches.The issue gets more intriguing when viewed alongside the composition of the selection committees. Documents accessed by TOI show Col Sandeep Dewan, Jai Rathore (who also goes by the name Mrityunjay Sinh Rathore and Jay Rathore) and Kapil Modi were on the dressage selection committee, while Col Amit Sinsinwar and Imitiaz Anees were on the three-day eventing selection committee. Dewan and Imitiaz were also part of the technical committee.Several of these officials are now travelling with the contingent. The sanctioned coaching/support staff included Anees, Rathore and Sinsinwar as coaches, with Dewan as team leader.Sources said the overlap between those involved in selecting the Asian Games team and those accompanying it has raised questions about a potential conflict of interest, though there is no suggestion of wrongdoing against any individual.The issue is particularly pointed in Shruti’s case. Sources said the dressage rider has written to the authorities stating that Rathore has not coached her and that she has been trained by Moody. She has sought Moody’s accreditation instead.There is also the Sinsinwar episode. India’s show jumping squad was dropped after failing to meet the selection criteria, leaving the country to compete only in dressage and three-day eventing. Yet Sinsinwar, nominated as show jumping coach, was initially included in the sanctioned contingent.The anomaly was subsequently corrected. In a mail accessed by TOI, the IOA told EFI’s ad-hoc committee that Sinsinwar was “not to be deputed to Japan” as the show jumping team had not been approved, and directed that his accreditation card be returned.The personal-coach issue, however, remains alive.In the same communication, the IOA said it was “taking the necessary steps” with the OCA and AINAGOC regarding the five personal coaches and getting them accreditation.Interestingly, EFI’s ad-hoc committee had separately recommended just two — Moody and Bierlein — saying they could also coach other members of the team.The questions now are hard to ignore: why were coaches sought by riders not part of the original support structure, why are officials involved in selection also travelling with the team, and was the initial coaching list the result of oversight — or simply the federation’s recommendation being accepted without enough scrutiny?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Denver Summit down first-place Gotham at home 3-0
articles.summary: Yazmeen Ryan scored against her former team and Kat Asman made four crucial saves in the Denver Summit's 3-0 win on Sunday over visiting Gotham FC in the Nat...
articles.body:
Yazmeen Ryan scored against her former team and Kat Asman made four crucial saves in the Denver Summit's 3-0 win on Sunday over visiting Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League.

In the day's other matches, the North Carolina Courage stunned the Chicago Stars 6-0; the Washington Spirit came from behind to beat the Portland Thorns 2-1; the Orlando Pride overtook the Houston Dash 3-1; and the Seattle Reign beat the San Diego Wave 1-0.

Gotham (13-4-6) has sat atop the National Women's Soccer League standings for six weeks, with its last loss coming July 4 against the Wave. The expansion Summit had already beaten Gotham once this season, recording the first win in franchise history 2-0.

Denver (8-8-6) opened the scoring in the 50th minute when Yuzuki Yamamoto connected on the volley from Ayo Oke.

Rookie Olivia Thomas extended Denver's lead in the 82nd minute, driving into the box before ripping a shot past goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger.

Six minutes later, Ryan sent a shot to the bottom left corner out of Berger's reach.

Ashley Sanchez had a hat trick in North Carolina's 6-0 rout of the Stars (5-17-1) in Evanston, Illinois and now leads the league's Golden Boot race with 18 goals.

Sanchez, lurking at Chicago goalkeeper Kailen Sheridan's back post, capitalized on a cross and knocked a ball that was pinging around the box into the back of the net in the 11th minute.

Just six minutes later, Chioma Okafor pushed the lead to 2-0 with her first NWSL goal.

The Courage (12-8-3) combined for three goals in eight minutes in the second half. Shinomi Koyama scored in the 61st minute and two minutes later, Ryan Williams collected a rebound and put it away to make it 4-0.

Sanchez converted a penalty before capping her hat trick with a header off a cross from Williams. in the 81st minute

Bethi caps first Spirit start with winner

Mélissa Bethi scored her first league goal in her first start for the Spirit in the 80th minute in Portland.

Trinity Rodman beat the defenders down the sideline and crossed to Bethi for the goal.

The Thorns (11-7-5) set the tone early when Sophia Wilson converted a penalty in the 18th minute. Portland was awarded the kick after Monique Ngock pulled down Thorns midfielder Nina Nijstad in the box.

The Spirit (13-6-4) leveled the match in the 59th minute when Nijstad committed a foul against Bethi in the penalty box. After video review, Tara Rudd stepped up to score the lick.

Washington's Andi Sullivan was ejected in the seventh minute of stoppage time after a rough tackle just outside the penalty area.

Banda breaks Marta's single-season scoring record for the Pride

Barbra Banda made Orlando Pride history Sunday, converting a 42nd-minute penalty to become the club's single-season scoring leader.

Her 14th goal of the season surpassed Marta's record set in 2017, as the Pride went on to defeat the Houston Dash 3-1 in Orlando.

Banda's record-setting goal capped a first half in which Orlando took advantage of early Houston mistakes. Dash rookie Leah Klenke put the Pride ahead with an own goal in the 14th minute before conceding a penalty against Summer Yates 28 minutes later.

Banda sent her shot into the bottom left corner past goalkeeper Jane Campbell, giving Orlando a 2-0 lead heading into halftime.

Banda has scored in eight different home appearances this season, a feat achieved by only four players in NWSL history.

Orlando (9-12-2) stretched its advantage in the 64th minute on Haley McCutcheon's goal.

Houston (7-11-5) scored less than 10 minutes later when Khyah Harper's cross found Kiki Van Zanten, who headed the ball past goalkeeper Cosette Morché.

Maddie Mercado finished off a lofted cross from Maddie Dahlien with a header for a goal in the Reign's win at home.

Seattle (10-8-4) played with a player advantage over San Diego (12-8-3) for much of the match after Wave defender Amelia Van Zanten was shown a red card in the 13th minute. Van Zanten was sent off for a tackle from behind on Dahlien.

Reign goalkeeper Claudia Dickey made six saves before exiting the match following a collision with Wave forward Ludmila. Cassie Miller helped preserve Seattle's clean sheet.

articles.title: Who Won The NASCAR Cup Series Southern 500 at Darlington? Full Race Results
articles.summary: Christopher Bell opened The Chase for the NASCAR Cup Series by earning his first victory of the 2026 season. After passing Kyle Larson for the lead with 12 c...
articles.body:
Christopher Bell opened The Chase for the NASCAR Cup Series by earning his first victory of the 2026 season. After passing Kyle Larson for the lead with 12 circuits remaining, Bell captured the victory in Sunday night's Cook Out Southern 500 at the Darlington Raceway.

It was Bell's first Darlington win, first victory of the 2026 season and 14th career Cup win overall. The win was huge for Bell's championship hopes as he moved into the second position in the standings, 12 points behind leader Denny Hamlin.

It was a trying evening for Hamlin, who entered the Chase as the top seed. In the final stage, contact between Hamlin and Michael McDowell caused toe link damage on the No. 11 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota.

The contact forced Hamlin to go a lap behind. The 45-year-old gained his lap back and ultimately finished 18th. Going into Darlington, Hamlin had a 25-point lead over second place Ryan Blaney. Now, the JGR driver has a 12-point edge over Bell.

William Byron had a difficult evening at Darlington as he posted a DNF of 37th place. The driver of the No. 24 suffered a flat tire in the final stage, then suffered an engine failure on the subsequent restart.

Full NASCAR Cup Series Darlington Southern 500 results

Key NASCAR Cup takeaways from New Hampshire

Stage 1 ended with Brad Keselowski spinning out after contact with Carson Hocevar

Tyler Reddick won Stage 1 and finished third.

Reddick lost ground during Stage 2 after a pit road miscue

Christopher Bell won Stage 2, earning 10 points.

Hamlin suffers toe link issue after contact with Michael McDowell in the final stage

Zane Smith spun out on Lap 283, triggering a caution

William Byron suffered an engine failure in the final stage and finished 37th

The race start time was bumped up 10 minutes due to the threat of rain

The race had a brief red flag for rain with 30 laps remaining

articles.title: Elly De La Cruz turns 'part-time bird whisperer' during Reds' win
articles.summary: The Reds' Elly De La Cruz helped a bird struggling to get off the field and brought it to safety during Cincinnati's win against Milwaukee at GABP.
articles.body:
The Reds' Elly De La Cruz came to the rescue of a bird struggling to get off the field and brought it to safety during the fourth inning of Cincinnati's series-concluding win against the Milwaukee Brewers at Great American Ball Park.

"Elly De La Cruz: full-time baseball player, part-time bird whisperer," the Reds tweeted with video.

When De La Cruz homered in the bottom half of the same inning, the Reds tweeted , "Bye bye birdie."

Sal Stewart, Reds visit Ja'Marr Chase, Cincinnati Bengals training camp

"How about that? He does it all," manager Terry Francona said of De La Cruz's rescue.
